hard.note: the exception for very complex work, but BUDGET-CAPPED at an absolute $3.00/M: only models on hard_whitelist may be routed, and nothing dearer than the cap is present in this file (the closed frontier seats - gemini-4-argon $12/M, gpt-5.3-codex $15.75/M, muse-wonder $24/M - were removed on Luke's directive 2026-10-28). policy.rejected_reason: Rejected 2026-11-16 at 5.47x the baseline ($4.100/M vs the list's own $0.750/M baseline at baseline_price_usd_per_m) for a medium coding turn; the suggested pool order put it first. The ratio is checkable inside THIS FILE at any time: the rejected entry for kimi-k2.7-code stores in_usd_per_m and out_usd_per_m whose sum IS its price_usd_per_m, and price_usd_per_m / baseline_price_usd_per_m IS its ratio_of_baseline (the entry is re-priced by every daily scan; it read 0.60 + 3.00 = $3.600/M = 4.8x on 2026-11-21). kimi is deliberately absent from this file's prices block because it is rejected by policy, not routed.
policy.rule: Every pool must LEAD with a model cheaper than the baseline. Every model in a SIMPLE pool is cheaper than the baseline. A medium pool may carry the baseline as the in-pool fallback. `hard` may lead dearer - that is the exception for very complex work - but only from the hard whitelist and never above $3.00/M.

amazon-bedrock.reason: Rejects replayed reasoning content: HTTP 400 'Provider returned error' with raw 'User messages cannot contain reasoning content. Please remove the reasoning content and try again.' The client's sanitizer returns early for non-assistant roles and its self-heal only matches UNKNOWN-FIELD phrasings, so the rejection is never recorded, the route is never narrowed, and every reasoning-bearing turn pays one wasted NON-retryable round-trip plus a user-visible fallback. Excluding the upstream is correct even though a single-upstream model would then have zero providers: with several upstreams the request simply lands on a usable one.
amazon-bedrock.evidence: docs/evidence/ + skills/devops/hermes-model-config/references/model-upstream-servability.md (probe: curl -s https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models/<m>/endpoints); operator directive 2026-11-17 'You can ignore all Amazon bedrock'
amazon-bedrock.scope: all models - the incompatibility is a property of the upstream's request validation, not of one model

free_tier_policy.note: The fleet only wants USEFUL free-tier models — the deepseek-flash class (cheap, general-purpose text/code chat). The daily scan (orch-model-market-scan.py) classifies free-tier candidates by ID token: a free model whose id contains a junk token (audio/specialty — e.g. google/lyria-3-pro-preview, a music model) is dropped from the unvetted alert and recorded in state free_tier_junk_dropped; a free model that does not (e.g. google/gemma-4-31b-it:free) stays a candidate. Paid candidates are untouched. Classification is id-based so it is deterministic across the live catalog and the cache fallback. Routing still excludes *:free (router-pools-seed.py) — this policy gates the ALERT, not the route; enabling free models in pools is a separate operator decision.

effort.note: trivial->low, routine->low, substantial->medium, expert->high. Chosen over [none,low,medium,high] because none on a confident-trivial tool-needing turn is the recorded regression (upstream jevkit/effort.py: a live fleet turn answered without calling a single tool when thinking was off); low on trivial buys most of the saving without that failure. One config value flips back if the operator wants none.
